data.long_meaning: From the Greek word hepsibō, meaning 'dedicated to God'. In the Bible, there is a woman named Hepsibah mentioned in Jeremiah 31:22.

biblical_reference.note: Hepsibah was the daughter of Abitur and the wife of Barzillai. She lived in Ribbonah. When David fled from Absalom, she took care of him and his men.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hepsiba has its roots in Greek mythology and Biblical history. In ancient Greece, Hepsibō was a name dedicated to the god Apollo, signifying dedication to the divine. In the Bible, Hepsibah is a woman who represents hope and restoration, as she is mentioned in Jeremiah 31:22 in relation to the return of Israelites to their homeland after exile.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hepsiba holds deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of dedication to God and the promise of hope and restoration. It can serve as a reminder for individuals to remain committed to their faith and trust in God's plan, even during difficult times. The name also represents the transformative power of God, as seen in the biblical reference to Hepsibah being mentioned in the context of the Israelites returning home after exile.

historical_references.reference: In ancient Greek, Hepsiba is derived from the word "heptos", meaning seven, and "bia", meaning life.
historical_references.context: In ancient Greek mythology, Hepsiba was the name of a nymph who was associated with the number seven.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Hepsiba remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
